summary: Per-block PPL attribution under cycle 221's 6-block joint Adam fit (BLOCKS=[1,2,4,5,7,8], K=512). Refit seed 42 to regenerate the W_out/b_out snapshot (no .pt on disk), then restore each compressed block's float MLP one at a time to decompose the 53.895 -> 59.515 PPL gap.
strengths: Cheap analysis cycle: ~10 min refit + 6 swap-and-eval rounds, no new optimisation regime.
Pre-flight verified cycle 221 logs lack tensor snapshot; refit budget acknowledged upfront.
Restore-roundtrip assert (eval after un-swap matches fully_compressed_ppl to 1e-4) catches aliasing bugs.
Non-additivity of per-block deltas explicitly noted as expected, not failure.
Two complementary measurements: PPL deltas (output-side) and residual MSE (input-side).
Pre-registered verdict thresholds prevent post-hoc reframing.
concerns: Refit nondeterminism on MPS: 0.05 PPL tolerance vs cycle 221's 59.391 is tight but defensible (same seed, same data order, same device).
Phase 3 re-runs collect_mlp_io twice; minor inefficiency, could cache calib activations from Phase 0. Not blocking.
Holding float + compressed model simultaneously is fine for GPT-2 small; OOM fallback (model_float to CPU) is in place.
risks: If refit lands >0.3 PPL from cycle 221 reference, decomposition is on a different operating point. Plan handles by recording actual baseline.
If contributions are uniform (REFUTED branch), headline becomes 'no bottleneck, 6.0 PPL distributed' — still a valid negative result.
optional_suggestions: Cache calib activations once during Phase 0 to skip the second collect_mlp_io pass in Phase 3.
